title: Tours & Awards
text:
Noah Kahan’s live career scaled dramatically alongside the success of Stick Season. What began as support slots and small venue headline dates grew into sold-out arena and amphitheater tours as the album found a global audience.


Early Years — Plays clubs and small theaters, opening for other artists while building a fanbase.


2022–2023 — Headlines the Stick Season Tour, growing from theaters to larger venues as the album’s popularity surges.


2023 — Performs at major festivals, including sets that introduce his folk-pop sound to broader festival audiences.


2024 — Headlines the We’ll All Be Here Forever Tour, playing arenas and stadiums across North America, the UK, and Europe.

title: Welcome

Folk-pop singer-songwriter from Strafford, Vermont

“I’m not much of a romantic, I’m as cold as the water in the pool up in Vermont” — Stick Season

title: Welcome
text:
About the Artist
Noah Kahan is an American singer-songwriter whose blend of folk instrumentation, self-deprecating lyricism, and pop songcraft turned him into one of the breakout artists of the 2020s. Raised in Strafford, Vermont, Kahan built a devoted online following before his 2022 album Stick Season became a cultural phenomenon, soundtracking a wave of interest in “New England sad-boy” folk-pop and earning him a Grammy nomination for Best New Artist.
His songwriting leans on the specifics of small-town New England life — snow, homesickness, strained family relationships, and the ache of growing up — set against arrangements that borrow as much from The Lumineers and Mumford & Sons as from mainstream pop radio.


🎸 Genre
Folk-pop, indie folk, pop


📍 Hometown
Strafford, Vermont


🏆 Recognition

title: Biography
text: Noah Kahan was born in 1997 and raised in Strafford, Vermont, a small rural town he has described as central to both his identity and his songwriting. Music was part of his household growing up, and he began writing songs and posting them online as a teenager, building a following on platforms like YouTube and SoundCloud before he had a record deal.

Music was part of his household growing up, and he began writing songs and posting them online as a teenager, building a following on platforms like YouTube and SoundCloud before he had a record deal.

title: Biography
text:
Getting Discovered
Kahan’s early single “Young Blood” caught the attention of Republic Records, leading to a record deal while he was still a teenager. He spent his late teens and early twenties developing his sound, releasing music that leaned closer to conventional pop before returning to the folk and acoustic influences of his childhood.

title: Biography
text:
Breaking Through

“Stick season, it’s already got its icy grip on me” — the opening line that launched a thousand playlists.

His 2021 EP Cape Elizabeth signaled a turn toward the introspective, New England-rooted sound that would define his career. That shift crystallized with the 2022 release of his third studio album, Stick Season, named for the bleak stretch of late autumn in northern New England after the leaves have fallen and before the snow arrives. The album — and its title track in particular — went viral on TikTok and streaming platforms, resonating with listeners far outside Vermont who connected with its themes of homesickness, arrested development, and small-town restlessness.

title: Biography
text:
The Stick Season Era
Kahan followed the album with deluxe reissues (Stick Season (We’ll All Be Here Forever) and Stick Season (Forever)), packed with additional tracks and high-profile collaborations, including “Northern Attitude” with Zach Bryan and “Call Your Mom” with Lizzy McAlpine. The extended rollout kept the project in the cultural conversation for nearly two years, moving him from small clubs to headlining arenas and festivals worldwide.

title: Biography
text:
Timeline


1997 — Born in Vermont.


Teens — Signs with Republic Records after early singles gain attention online.


2019 — Releases debut album Busyhead.


2021 — Releases I Was / I Am and the Cape Elizabeth EP, moving toward a folk-driven sound.


2022 — Releases Stick Season, his commercial breakthrough.


2023 — Releases deluxe editions We’ll All Be Here Forever and Forever; launches The Busyhead Project.


2024 — Nominated for a Grammy Award for Best New Artist; headlines major festivals and arena tours.


Learn more about his music on the Discography page, or his touring history on Tours & Awards.

title: Discography
text:
Notable Songs


“Stick Season”
The title track and signature hit — a wistful account of heartbreak and homesickness set against the Vermont autumn.


“Dial Drunk”
A frenetic, radio-friendly single about a late-night drunk call to an ex; later reworked as a duet with Post Malone.


“Northern Attitude”
A collaboration with Zach Bryan reflecting on the guardedness bred by a cold-weather upbringing.


“You’re Gonna Go Far”
An anthemic, string-laden track about watching someone you love outgrow their hometown.


“Call Your Mom”
A tender duet with Lizzy McAlpine about checking in on the people you love during hard times.


“Homesick”
An earlier fan favorite that captures the pull between wanting to leave a small town and never wanting to leave it.

title: Philanthropy
text:
In 2023, Noah Kahan launched The Busyhead Project, a mental health initiative named after his 2019 debut album Busyhead. The project reflects Kahan’s own openness about his experiences with anxiety and depression, which he has discussed candidly in interviews and woven throughout his songwriting.
Through the initiative, Kahan has directed proceeds from portions of his tour and merchandise sales toward mental health organizations, aiming to reduce stigma and expand access to mental health resources — particularly for young people and touring musicians, a population that faces unique pressures on the road.

title: Philanthropy
text:
Advocacy Through Music
Kahan’s lyrics frequently touch on mental health, family strain, and the difficulty of asking for help, themes that resonated strongly with fans navigating similar struggles. Songs like “Growing Sideways” and “False Confidence” directly reference his experience with therapy and anxiety, helping normalize those conversations for a mainstream pop audience.

“I wanted to make something that gave back to the community that helped raise me, and to a cause that’s been such a huge part of my life and my music.” — on the founding of The Busyhead Project

title: Philanthropy
text:
Getting Involved
Fans interested in supporting mental health causes connected to Kahan’s advocacy can look for Busyhead Project fundraising campaigns tied to his tours, or support mental health organizations directly in their own communities.
